homepage.content: Make it easier for others to track your work and cite what you make
homepage.accordion_summary_1:
A record is a structured, machine-readable metadata file that describes your work in a standardized way. By using widely adopted data and metadata standards, records make your projects easier to understand, share, and integrate across systems. They help ensure your work is discoverable, reusable, and compatible with research infrastructure and data catalogues.

With records, you can document almost anything—projects, datasets, data schemas, sample libraries, workflows, and more. Each record captures essential details about your work and expresses them in a consistent format that other tools and platforms can interpret.

The record tool includes a library of built-in schemas, letting you write metadata that follows specific community or organizational standards. Every record is generated as JSON, making it easy to integrate into existing systems, automate workflows, and maintain interoperability across your data ecosystem.

viewhelppage.intro: This page displays a read-only summary of your catalogue record before you download or publish it.
viewhelppage.step1_body: Check every section carefully. Fields with no value show a placeholder message. Click Edit at the bottom to return to the form and make changes.
viewhelppage.step2_body: Add optional revision notes describing what changed. When revising a published record, a new immutable SAID is generated while preserving lineage to the previous record.
viewhelppage.step3_body: Use Download (.json) to save a standards-compliant JSON-LD file with a deterministic SAID, or click Update to ContextHub when launched from ContextHub.

formhelppage.intro: Use this page to fill in or update metadata fields defined by the selected catalogue schema.
formhelppage.step1_body: Use the filter pills in the left sidebar to switch between Mandatory fields only, Recommended fields, or the Complete schema. Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are required.
formhelppage.step2_body: Click Add to create repeatable entries such as contributors or identifiers. Inside a nested item form, click Save to keep your entry or Cancel to discard changes.
formhelppage.step3_body: For contributor ORCID fields, use Search ORCID Registry to look up researchers by name or affiliation and auto-fill their ORCID iD and name. Once all required fields are valid, click Review to preview and export your record.
